nodes.title: Hyperbolic area on quotient charts
nodes.statement: For a torsion-free cocompact discrete projective group Γ, descend the curvature −1 disc form to X=Γ\D and construct its Borel area measure. nodes.title: Compact injectivity radius
nodes.statement: For a torsion-free cocompact Γ acting on D with curvature −1 distance, ρ_X=inf_{z∈D,γ∈Γ\{1}}d₁(z,γz)/2, equivalently half the shortest closed geodesic length. nodes.title: Positive diagonal potential comparison
nodes.statement: On D², μ=χ/(1+√(1−χ))² is smooth, including Δ, and F=−8πlog(1−μ) is smooth psh. Extend log μ by −∞ on Δ; it is psh and locally integrable. The coefficient matrix of ddᶜF is [[2−t,−1/t],[−1/t,(2−t)/t⁴]], whereas ω−ddᶜF has matrix [[t,1/t],[1/t,1/t³]]. These matrices are semipositive for 0<t≤1; the latter has rank one.

For h(s)=log((1−√(1−s))/(1+√(1−s))), h′=1/(s√(1−s)), h″=(3s−2)/(2s²(1−s)^(3/2)). Substitute to obtain the displayed rank-one log μ Hessian. For F the derivative is 4π/((1−s)(1+√(1−s))); substitution gives the displayed ddᶜ matrix and complement. Principal minors establish both inequalities.

A common disc automorphism sends any (z,w) to (0,w′); holomorphic covariance transports semipositivity. The algebraic expression μ=χ/(1+√(1−χ))² proves smoothness through χ=0 and extends F inequalities by continuity.

For log μ write log χ−2log(1+√(1−χ)); its singular part is log|z−w|². Away from Δ positivity holds by the matrix; upper extension across this analytic hypersurface and Poincaré–Lelong supply positivity including the divisor atom. No scalar value Real.log 0 is used as the extended potential.

The complement matrix has zero determinant, while the F matrix determinant is 4(1−t)/t⁴; both diagonal entries are positive.

nodes.title: Gonality of the smooth projective model
